statement: A function of several real variables (or real multivariate function) is a function $f: D \to \mathbb{R}$ (or vector-valued $f: D \to \mathbb{R}^m$) with more than one argument ($n > 1$), where all input arguments are real variables $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n) \in D$ and the domain $D$ is a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

symbols.dimensions: D subset of R^n -> R (or R^m)

symbols.meaning: vector of real input variables (x_1, x_2, ..., x_n)
dimension of the output space for vector-valued multivariate functions

properties.property: Separate continuity in each individual argument does not imply multivariate continuity
properties.why: a function may be continuous along each coordinate axis while failing to be continuous along arbitrary continuous paths $s(t)$

properties.property: Differentiability in a neighborhood of a point implies continuity at that point, but the converse is not true
properties.why: the linear approximation $f(\mathbf{x}) = f(\mathbf{a}) + \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{a}) \cdot (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{a}) + \alpha(\mathbf{x})|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{a}|$ with $\alpha(\mathbf{x}) \to 0$ guarantees that $f(\mathbf{x}) \to f(\mathbf{a})$ as $|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{a}| \to 0$

properties.property: Differentiability at a point implies the existence of all first-order partial derivatives at that point
properties.why: the components of the linear approximation vector $A_i(\mathbf{a})$ equal the partial derivatives $\left.\frac{\partial f(\mathbf{x})}{\partial x_i}\right|_{\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{a}}$

properties.property: A partial derivative of a multivariable function is a derivative with respect to one variable with all other variables held constant
properties.why: it corresponds to the directional derivative of the function along a coordinate axis

properties.property: A non-zero gradient vector $\nabla f(\mathbf{a})$ is perpendicular to the level hypersurface $f(\mathbf{x}) = c$
properties.why: the total differential along the level set vanishes identically, giving $df = \nabla f \cdot d\mathbf{x} = 0$

properties.property: A function has differentiability class $C^p$ if all order $p$ partial derivatives exist and are continuous throughout the domain
properties.why: continuity of all order $p$ partial derivatives defines class $C^p$, with $C^\infty$ denoting smoothness

properties.property: Definite integration extends to multiple integration over a Cartesian product region $R = R_1 \times R_2 \times \dots \times R_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$
properties.why: the multiple integral is evaluated iteratively as $\int_{R_n} \dots \int_{R_1} f(x_1, \dots, x_n) dx_1 \dots dx_n \equiv \int_R f(\mathbf{x}) d^n\mathbf{x}$

assumptions.assumption: The function possesses multiple real-valued arguments ($n > 1$)
assumptions.breaks_when: The domain is one-dimensional ($n = 1$) or variables are non-real without decomposition into real and imaginary parts

assumptions.assumption: Coordinates are defined in an $n$-dimensional rectangular Cartesian coordinate system with unit scale factors and metric tensor equal to the Kronecker delta
assumptions.breaks_when: Curvilinear coordinate systems are used, requiring metric tensor scale factors in the gradient and differential operators

failure_modes.mode: Failure of multivariate continuity despite existence of separate one-variable continuity
failure_modes.signature: Limits along coordinate axes exist and match $f(\mathbf{x}_0)$, but the multivariate limit along another continuous path $s(t)$ (such as $x=t, y=t$) does not equal $f(\mathbf{x}_0)$
failure_modes.cause: Multivariate continuity requires convergence across all continuous curves through $\mathbf{x}_0$, which is not implied by continuity along coordinate axes alone

failure_modes.mode: Failure of differentiability despite existence of all partial derivatives
failure_modes.signature: Partial derivatives $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}$ exist at $\mathbf{a}$, but the error term $\alpha(\mathbf{x})|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{a}|$ does not satisfy $\alpha(\mathbf{x}) \to 0$ as $|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{a}| \to 0$
failure_modes.cause: The existence of directional derivatives along coordinate directions does not guarantee the existence of a valid linear approximating hyperplane in a full neighborhood of $\mathbf{a}$

failure_modes.signature: The quotient function $f/g$ is undefined or fails to be continuous at $\mathbf{x}_0$
failure_modes.cause: The denominator function vanishes at the evaluation point ($g(\mathbf{x}_0) = 0$)
